name: Dedication of the Lateran Basilica
history: Saint John Lateran, not Saint Peter's, is the cathedral of the Pope as Bishop of Rome, 'mother and head of all the churches of the city and the world'. It was dedicated by Pope Sylvester in 324, soon after the Church was freed from persecution.
meditation: You are God's temple. Pray for your own parish church and its priest today.
life: The Lateran takes its name from the Laterani, a Roman family whose palace passed to the emperor Constantine. After he ended the persecution, Constantine gave the property to the Bishop of Rome, and a great basilica was built beside it and dedicated to Christ the Saviour; later the two Saints John, the Baptist and the Evangelist, were added to its title. For about a thousand years the popes lived at the Lateran, and five general councils of the Church met there, including the Fourth Lateran Council of 1215. The basilica has been ruined by earthquake and fire and rebuilt more than once; its present façade dates from the eighteenth century. The feast was extended to the whole Church as a sign of love and unity with the See of Peter.
prayerTo: Lord God, you build your Church from living stones, chosen and precious. As we honour the cathedral of the Bishop of Rome, unite us more closely with the Holy Father and with one another. Make my own heart a fit dwelling for your Spirit, and keep every parish church a house of prayer for all peoples. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
penance: Pray for the Pope today, and make a visit to your parish church. Give something towards its upkeep or its work for the poor.
